mainTopic: The end of the questions about partly cancelling an 'except' restriction, and the four זקנים's arguments against רבי אליעזר's partial גט and their refutations
overview: The amud opens by finishing a set of questions about a husband who wrote 'except ראובן and שמעון' in a גט and then took back only part of it. The questions about naming only one of them, or saying 'also to שמעון', end with תיקו. Next comes a ברייתא: after רבי אליעזר died, four זקנים came to argue against his view that a גט forbidding the woman to one man is valid. רבי טרפון points to blocked יבום, רבי יוסי הגלילי says nothing is forbidden to one man and permitted to another, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה reads כריתות as a full cutting-off, and רבי עקיבא raises the risk of ממזרים and a קל וחומר about a כהן. רבי יהושע objects that one does not refute a lion after his death. רבא rules that every argument except רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's has a weak point, and a ברייתא quoting רבי יוסי agrees. The גמרא then goes through the arguments one by one, names the weak point in each, and works out whether each was aimed at a גט worded 'except' (חוץ) or 'on condition' (על מנת). The amud ends in the middle of this check for רבי עקיבא's כהן argument, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What if he later permits only ראובן?
steps.stepSummary: Assuming the husband can take back his restriction, the גמרא asks what happens if he later says only 'to ראובן'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we say that what he forbade he can permit again, what if he later said 'to ראובן'? Did he mean ראובן and also שמעון, and he named ראובן only because ראובן came first? Or did he mean ראובן alone?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues an earlier line of thought. It now asks a new question: if the husband took back the restriction but named only ראובן, is שמעון also permitted?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the husband forbade two men, ראובן and שמעון. Now he names only ראובן. One side says naming ראובן was just a short way of cancelling the whole list, since ראובן was the first name in it. The other side says he meant ראובן and nobody else.

keyTerms.meaning: What he forbade, he permitted (he can undo his own restriction)
What is the law? (opens a question)
And the same is true for...
Because he opened with him (he was named first)
Or perhaps (introduces the other side of a question)
Specifically, only this and nothing more

phrases.english: [if you say] what he forbade, he permitted;
phrases.notes: This finishes a line from the page before: he first forbade ראובן and שמעון, and later took that back.

phrases.english: if he said 'to ראובן,' what is the law?
Does 'to ראובן' mean the same is true for שמעון,
and the reason he said 'to ראובן'
is because he opened with him;
or perhaps he meant specifically ראובן?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the chain of questions begun on the previous page about a husband who takes back his restriction.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When the husband takes back his restriction and names only ראובן, does that also free her to marry שמעון?

steps.title: What if he later permits only שמעון?
steps.stepSummary: If naming ראובן means only ראובן, then what if he names שמעון, the last name on the list?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say 'to ראובן' means only ראובן, what if he said 'to שמעון'? Did he mean שמעון and also ראובן, and he named שמעון only because שמעון was the last name he had said? Or did he mean שמעון alone?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds a second question on top of the first. Even if we decide that 'ראובן' means only ראובן, maybe naming the last person on the list works differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is an 'if you say' chain. Naming the first person might be read narrowly. But naming the last person might still mean the whole list, because people often repeat the last word they just said.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say (the next question assumes one answer to the previous one)
Because he ended with him (he was named last)

phrases.english: And if you say 'to ראובן' means specifically ראובן;
if he said 'to שמעון,' what is the law?
Does 'to שמעון' mean the same is true for ראובן,
and the reason he said 'שמעון'
is because he ended with him;
phrases.notes: In his first statement, 'except ראובן and שמעון', שמעון was the last name he said.

phrases.english: or perhaps he meant specifically שמעון?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes the narrow answer to Step 1 and asks a follow-up question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: If naming the first person means only that person, does naming the last person (שמעון) also cover ראובן?

steps.title: רב אשי asks about 'also to שמעון'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks what the word 'also' adds in the phrase 'also to שמעון'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: if he said 'also to שמעון,' what is the law? Does 'also' mean 'in addition to ראובן'? Or does 'also' mean 'in addition to everyone else'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks one more question about the same case. This time the husband said 'also to שמעון,' and the question is what 'also' points back to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'also' points to ראובן, he is saying 'ראובן, and also שמעון,' so both are permitted. If 'also' points to 'everyone,' he only added שמעון to the people already allowed, and ראובן stays forbidden.

phrases.english: רב אשי asked:
if he said 'also to שמעון,' what is the law?
Does 'also' refer to ראובן?
Or perhaps 'also' refers to everyone else?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new wording question about the same case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'also' in 'also to שמעון' include ראובן, or only add שמעון to everyone else who is already permitted?

steps.title: The question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends the question with תיקו: no answer is found.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes רב אשי's question without an answer. The question is left open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו does not mean either side is wrong. It means the גמרא could not prove which reading is correct, so the doubt remains.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question stays unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: None of the questions about how the husband takes back his restriction is answered. Each one ends as a doubt.
steps.confusionAlert: תיקו is not a ruling for either side. It means the גמרא found no proof, and the question remains open.

phrases.english: Let it stand unanswered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רב אשי's question without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The meaning of 'also to שמעון' remains in doubt.

steps.title: Four זקנים come to answer רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that after רבי אליעזר died, four great זקנים came to answer his position.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: after רבי אליעזר died, four elders came in to answer his words. They were רבי יוסי הגלילי, רבי טרפון, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, and רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new section by quoting a ברייתא. It sets up the arguments that the four זקנים will bring against רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אליעזר holds that a גט saying 'permitted to everyone except so-and-so' is valid. This ברייתא introduces four חכמים who will challenge that view. Their actual arguments come next.

keyTerms.meaning: To answer and challenge his words

steps.whyThisMatters: The arguments of these four זקנים, coming next, explain why the חכמים do not accept רבי אליעזר's view.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
After the death of Rabbi Eliezer,
four elders entered
to respond to his words,
and these are they: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן, וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon, Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya,
and Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לְאַחַר פְּטִירָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section, going back to the main dispute in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four זקנים set out to challenge רבי אליעזר's view; their arguments follow.

steps.title: רבי טרפון: The condition could block a Torah מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון argues that if the woman marries the brother of the forbidden man and he dies childless, the condition blocks יבום. That would uproot a Torah law, so such a גט cannot count as כריתות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי טרפון said: Suppose she marries the brother of the man she was forbidden to, and that brother dies with no children. The forbidden man should do יבום with her, but the first husband's condition stops him. So the first husband has uprooted a Torah law. This shows such a גט is not a real 'cutting off.'
steps.whatsHappening: The first of the four זקנים attacks רבי אליעזר's view. He builds a case where the husband's condition clashes with the מצוה of יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman's second husband dies childless, so his brother should do יבום. But that brother is the very man the first husband forbade her to marry. A גט that lets a private condition cancel a Torah מצוה cannot be what the Torah meant by כריתות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Cutting off.' The Torah's word for a גט (ספר כריתות), meaning a full separation
Uprooting something from the Torah, cancelling a Torah law
Levirate marriage. A man marries his brother's widow when the brother died with no children
She became forbidden to him because of the husband's condition

phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon responded and said:
Suppose this woman went

phrases.aramaic: וְנִישֵּׂאת לְאָחִיו שֶׁל זֶה שֶׁנֶּאֶסְרָה עָלָיו,
phrases.english: and married the brother of the man she was forbidden to
and he died without children —

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִמְצָא זֶה עוֹקֵר דָּבָר מִן הַתּוֹרָה?
phrases.english: isn't this one found to be uprooting something from the Torah?
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the first husband, the one who made the condition.

phrases.english: So you have learned that this is not 'cutting off.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first of the four זקנים introduced in step 5 gives his answer to רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's ruling that a גט with an 'except for so-and-so' condition is valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The condition can end up cancelling the Torah מצוה of יבום, and a valid גט cannot work that way.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: Nothing is forbidden to one man and permitted to another
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי argues that in Torah law, forbidden relationships are forbidden to everyone and permitted ones are permitted to everyone. A woman who is permitted to all men except one does not fit that pattern.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי said: Where do we ever find a woman forbidden to one man and permitted to another? What is forbidden is forbidden to all, and what is permitted is permitted to all. So this is not a real 'cutting off.'
steps.whatsHappening: The second זקן attacks רבי אליעזר's view with a general principle about how forbidden and permitted status works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's גט makes the woman free to marry every man except one. רבי יוסי הגלילי says the Torah never creates a status that is half forbidden and half permitted like this. A divorced woman must be fully free, so this גט fails.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Where do we find?' A way of saying there is no such case anywhere in Torah law

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili responded and said:

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכָן מָצִינוּ אָסוּר לָזֶה וּמוּתָּר לָזֶה?
phrases.english: Where do we find something forbidden to this one and permitted to that one?
What is forbidden is forbidden to everyone,
and what is permitted is permitted to everyone!
So you have learned that this is not 'cutting off.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate argument against רבי אליעזר from another of the four זקנים.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's ruling that a גט with an 'except for so-and-so' condition is valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Torah law has no status that is forbidden to one man yet permitted to all others, so the condition cannot create one.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: A גט must fully cut the bond
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה explains that the word כריתות means something that fully cuts between husband and wife. A גט that leaves the husband still controlling whom she may marry does not cut the bond.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said: 'כריתות' means something that cuts between him and her. So this is not a real 'cutting off.'
steps.whatsHappening: The third זקן argues from the meaning of the Torah's own word for a גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah calls a גט a 'ספר כריתות,' a document of cutting off. If the husband's condition still limits her after the divorce, a link to him remains, so nothing has really been cut.

phrases.aramaic: נַעֲנָה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה וְאָמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya responded and said:
'Severance' means something that cuts between him and her.
phrases.notes: He is reading the Torah's word for a גט, 'ספר כריתות' (דברים 24:1).

phrases.english: So you have learned that this is not 'cutting off.'

steps.triggerLanguage: נַעֲנָה רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה וְאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third argument against רבי אליעזר, this time from the meaning of the פסוק's word.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's ruling that a גט with an 'except for so-and-so' condition is valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word כריתות requires a complete cut, and the condition leaves a remaining tie between husband and wife.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: The condition could later cancel the גט and make children ממזרים
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא describes a woman who remarries, has children, and later marries the forbidden man. Her גט would then be cancelled after the fact, and her children from the second marriage would become ממזרים. So such a גט cannot be כריתות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: Suppose she married some ordinary man and had children with him. Then she was widowed or divorced, and she went ahead and married the man she was forbidden to. Wouldn't the גט turn out to be void, and her children be ממזרים? So this is not a real 'cutting off.'
steps.whatsHappening: The fourth and last זקן shows how the condition could cause a disaster years later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By marrying the forbidden man, she breaks the condition, so the גט falls apart. Looking back, she was still married to her first husband during her second marriage. That makes the children of the second marriage ממזרים, and a real גט cannot leave the outcome hanging like that.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Someone from the market,' an ordinary man
And she went ahead, ignoring the condition
Children born from a forbidden union, such as with a married woman

steps.whatToRemember: All four זקנים reach the same conclusion: a גט that forbids her to one man is not כריתות. So far they have given these reasons: blocking יבום, no partial forbidden status, the meaning of the word כריתות, and the risk of ממזרים. רבי עקיבא adds a second argument in the next steps.
steps.confusionAlert: The children are not from the forbidden man. They are from the ordinary second husband. They become ממזרים because the גט collapses, which means she was still married when she had them.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva responded and said:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָלְכָה זוֹ וְנִשֵּׂאת לְאֶחָד מִן הַשּׁוּק
phrases.english: Suppose this woman went and married an ordinary man
and she had children,
and she was widowed or divorced,
and she went ahead and married the one she was forbidden to —

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִמְצָא גֵּט בָּטֵל, וּבָנֶיהָ מַמְזֵרִים?
phrases.english: isn't the גט found to be void, and her children ממזרים?
So you have learned that this is not 'cutting off.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The fourth and final argument from the זקנים against רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's ruling that a גט with an 'except for so-and-so' condition is valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Breaking the condition later would cancel the גט after the fact and turn the children of her second marriage into ממזרים.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's second argument: the widow and the כהן
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא gives another case. The forbidden man is a כהן, and the husband who divorced her dies. Toward that כהן she is now an אלמנה, but toward everyone else she is a גרושה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another argument: suppose the man she was forbidden to is a כהן, and her ex-husband dies. Toward that כהן she counts as a widow, and toward everyone else she counts as a divorcée.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא opens a second attack on רבי אליעזר by describing a case. This step sets up the case, and the next step draws the conclusion from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Toward the one forbidden man, she was never really divorced, because the גט did not free her for him. So when the husband dies, she is a widow in relation to him. Everyone agrees she is still forbidden to this כהן, because she is a גרושה to the rest of the world.

keyTerms.meaning: A priest, who may not marry a divorcée

phrases.english: Another argument:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיָה זֶה שֶׁנֶּאֶסְרָה עָלָיו כֹּהֵן,
phrases.english: suppose the one she was forbidden to was a priest,
and the man who divorced her died,
is she not found to be a widow in relation to him,
phrases.notes: Toward this one man the גט never freed her, so she was still 'married' to him. The husband's death makes her a widow toward him.

phrases.english: and a divorcée in relation to everyone else?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי עקיבא's second argument, following his ממזרים argument in step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's view that a גט forbidding her to one man is valid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It sets up a case where she has a split status, so that the next step can show how a split status spreads.

steps.title: The קל וחומר: the married status should spread to everyone
steps.stepSummary: The light status of a divorcée still forbids her to that כהן. So the severe status of a married woman, which she has toward the one man, should surely forbid her to everyone. Therefore such a גט is not כריתות.
steps.simpleTranslation: A divorcée is a lighter prohibition, yet her divorced side forbids her even to the כהן who sees her as a widow. A married woman is a severe prohibition, so surely her married side forbids her to everyone. This shows that such a גט is not a real cutting-off.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא uses the case from step 10 to build a קל וחומר. He concludes that this kind of גט cannot count as כריתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her divorced status toward the world spreads and forbids her to the one כהן. Following that logic, her still-married status toward the one man should spread and forbid her to every man. In that case the גט would free her for no one, so it cannot be a real גט.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
A married woman, forbidden to all other men

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's second argument: a partial status spreads. If the light 'divorced' status spreads to the כהן, then the severe 'married' status should spread to everyone, and the גט accomplishes nothing.

phrases.english: And it is a kal vachomer:
just as a divorcée, which is a lighter prohibition,
is forbidden because of the divorced side in her;
a married woman, which is a severe prohibition,
is it not all the more so?!
phrases.notes: He means that her 'married' status toward the one man should forbid her to every man in the same way.

phrases.english: So you have learned that this is not a cutting-off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the case set up in step 10
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the light divorced status spreads, then by קל וחומר the severe married status spreads too. That would leave her forbidden to all men, so the גט is not כריתות.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: don't refute a lion after his death
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע objects to the whole exercise. One should not refute a great sage like רבי אליעזר after he has died.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to them: one does not refute a lion after his death.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע pushes back against the four זקנים. He says it is not right to knock down רבי אליעזר's view now that he can no longer answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע does not argue that the challenges are wrong on the facts. He is saying they cannot settle the matter, because רבי אליעזר might have had an answer if he were alive to give it.

keyTerms.meaning: A lion, here meaning a great sage

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע is not defending רבי אליעזר's ruling with a new reason. He only objects to refuting a sage who can no longer reply.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to them:
one does not refute the lion
after death.
phrases.notes: The 'lion' is רבי אליעזר. Once he is gone, he cannot defend his own view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to all four זקנים's challenges together
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: All four refutations, as a way of settling the question
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: They refute a sage who is no longer alive to answer them

steps.title: רבא: only רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's argument holds up
steps.stepSummary: רבא judges the four arguments. Each one can be challenged except the argument of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: all of them can be refuted, except for רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's argument, which cannot be refuted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא steps in to judge which of the four arguments against רבי אליעזר actually stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא says the arguments of רבי טרפון, רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא each have a weak point. Only רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's reading of the word כריתות, a full cutting-off, has no hole in it.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation, a hole in an argument

steps.whyThisMatters: This tells us which argument against רבי אליעזר is the strongest: the meaning of כריתות itself.

phrases.english: Rava said:
all of them have a refutation,
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means the answers of the four זקנים given above.

phrases.english: except for that of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya,
which has no refutation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כּוּלְּהוּ אִית לְהוּ פִּירְכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Evaluates the four arguments after רבי יהושע's objection
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's argument, that כריתות requires a complete cutting-off, cannot be refuted.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא: רבי יוסי prefers רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which רבי יוסי says he prefers רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's words over all the others. This supports רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This was also taught: רבי יוסי said, I prefer the words of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה over the words of all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבא's verdict with an earlier source, a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's choice is not only his own judgment. The תנא רבי יוסי already singled out רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's argument as the best of the four.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: Of the four זקנים, the argument that stands is רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's: a גט must fully cut the bond. Both רבא and רבי יוסי agree.

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
Rabbi Yosei said:
I see the words of
Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya
over the words of all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's verdict in step 13
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's argument is the strongest

steps.title: רבי טרפון's argument: the יבום problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי טרפון from the ברייתא. If the woman marries the brother of the man she was forbidden to, and that brother dies childless, the Torah's מצוה of יבום is uprooted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: רבי טרפון answered and said: Suppose this woman went and married the brother of the man she was forbidden to, and the brother died without children. Isn't the husband found to be uprooting a Torah law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back to the ברייתא and quotes the first argument, from רבי טרפון, so it can examine it closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman was divorced with a גט that forbids her to one particular man. She then marries that man's brother, and the brother dies with no children. Now the Torah wants the remaining brother to do יבום with her, but the גט made her forbidden to him, so the מצוה cannot happen.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said.' A formula the גמרא uses to quote a line from a ברייתא it just brought, so it can discuss it.
Uprooting a Torah law, making a Torah law unable to apply
Died without children, the situation that calls for יבום

phrases.english: The Master said,
Rabbi Tarfon responded and said:
Suppose this woman went and married
the brother of the one she was forbidden to,
and he died without children,
is this one not found
uprooting a matter of Torah law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר, נַעֲנָה רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן וְאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא to test the first of the four arguments that רבא said could be challenged.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט that forbids the woman to one man can block that man's future יבום, so it uproots a Torah law.

steps.title: Is the husband really the one uprooting?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the word 'uprooting.' The husband didn't do anything to the brother's marriage or death, so how is he uprooting anything?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Uprooting'? Is he the one who uproots it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the wording of רבי טרפון's argument. Calling the husband the 'uprooter' seems too strong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband only wrote a גט. The woman chose to marry the brother, and the brother died. The husband is not directly destroying the מצוה of יבום, so the word 'uprooting' doesn't fit him.

phrases.english: Uprooting?! Is he the one uprooting?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the exact word רבי טרפון used.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'עוקר' in רבי טרפון's argument
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The husband takes no direct action against the מצוה. Others' actions (her marriage, the brother's death) bring it about.

steps.title: New wording: he stipulates to uproot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords רבי טרפון: the husband is 'stipulating' (making a condition) that uproots a Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it as: 'he stipulates to uproot a Torah law.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording. The husband isn't uprooting by his own hands; his condition in the גט is what sets it up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The change moves the blame from a direct act to the condition the husband wrote. Since the condition is his, maybe the result is his fault.

phrases.english: Rather, "he stipulates to uproot
a matter of Torah law."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַתְנֶה לַעֲקוֹר דָּבָר מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by rewording the argument.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The husband himself uproots the Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The husband's condition in the גט is what uproots the Torah law.

steps.title: He never told her to marry the brother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges 'stipulating.' The husband's condition never required her to marry that man's brother. She chose that on her own.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Stipulating'? Did he tell her: 'It's not enough unless you marry that man's brother'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new wording too. The husband's condition only forbade one man; it said nothing about marrying his brother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A condition that 'uproots' the Torah would have to demand the problem itself. Here the condition only names who she can't marry. Marrying the brother was her own choice, so the husband's condition didn't uproot anything.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not enough / there is no way around it

phrases.english: Stipulating?! Did he say to her:
"It is not enough for you unless you marry
the brother of that man"?!
phrases.notes: He means the man the גט forbade her to. The husband never asked her to marry that man's brother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rewording just offered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The condition never required the marriage to the brother, so the condition itself does not uproot the מצוה.

steps.title: New wording: he causes the uprooting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords again: the husband 'causes' a Torah law to be uprooted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it as: 'he causes a Torah law to be uprooted.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a third, softer wording. The husband doesn't uproot or demand it, but his גט leads to it happening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the claim is only indirect. The husband set up a situation that may later block יבום. That is weaker than both earlier wordings, but it fits the facts.

phrases.english: Rather, "he causes to uproot
a matter of Torah law."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא גּוֹרֵם לַעֲקוֹר דָּבָר מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second challenge with a third wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The husband's condition directly uproots the Torah law.
steps.terutzMaskana: The husband only indirectly causes the Torah law to be uprooted.

steps.title: Then nobody could marry his niece
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges 'causing.' If indirectly causing is a problem, then a man shouldn't marry his brother's daughter, since if he dies childless, her father can't do יבום with his own daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Causing'? If so, a man should not marry his brother's daughter, in case he dies without children, and then he would be found causing a Torah law to be uprooted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the 'causing' idea goes too far. It would forbid something that is clearly allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a man marries his niece and dies childless, the one who should do יבום is his brother, her own father. A father can never marry his daughter, so יבום is blocked. No one forbids marrying a niece for this reason, so 'causing' alone can't be a reason to reject a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But if so, from now on…' Used to show an idea leads to a result nobody accepts

phrases.english: Causing?! But if that is so,
a man should not marry his brother's daughter,
lest he die without children,
phrases.notes: Then her father, his brother, would be the one to do יבום, but a father can't marry his own daughter.

phrases.english: and he will be found causing to uproot
a matter of Torah law!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the third wording by showing it leads to an unacceptable result.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that indirectly causing a Torah law to be blocked is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Marrying a niece also indirectly risks blocking יבום, yet it is allowed, so 'causing' cannot be a real objection.

steps.title: This is the weakness רבא meant
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the niece question is the refutation of רבי טרפון's argument that רבא was talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up: the niece case is exactly the challenge that makes רבי טרפון's argument weak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said every argument except רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's could be challenged. For רבי טרפון, the challenge is this one: indirectly causing יבום to be blocked is not a real problem, as the niece case shows.

keyTerms.meaning: This is / that is the same as
A refutation, a challenge that breaks an argument

steps.whatToRemember: רבי טרפון's argument fails because 'causing' a Torah law to be uprooted is not enough to reject a גט. Otherwise marrying one's niece would be forbidden too.

phrases.english: This is the refutation.
phrases.notes: He means the challenge רבא had in mind when he said these arguments could be knocked down (step 13).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the previous challenge as רבא's refutation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי טרפון's argument is refuted by the niece case.

steps.title: Which case was רבי טרפון talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which kind of גט רבי טרפון meant. It rules out the 'except so-and-so' case, because there רבי אליעזר lets her marry that man after she married someone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in which case? If you say it was a גט that says 'you may marry anyone except so-and-so,' רבי אליעזר permits her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question: what exact case did רבי טרפון mean? It rejects the first option right away and sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the 'except so-and-so' (חוץ) case, רבי אליעזר holds that once she married another man, she becomes permitted to the excluded man. So when the brother dies, she can do יבום with him, and רבי טרפון's problem doesn't exist. The גמרא must find a different case where his argument makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (offering a possible answer)
'Except', the גט that says 'you are permitted to all men except so-and-so'

phrases.english: And in what case?
If we say it was in a case of "except,"
Rabbi Eliezer permits her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After refuting רבי טרפון's reasoning, the גמרא asks what case his argument was even about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which type of conditional גט רבי טרפון's argument addresses.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading רבי טרפון as talking about the 'חוץ' case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In that case רבי אליעזר permits her to the excluded man after another marriage, so יבום is not blocked.

steps.title: Proof that the 'except so-and-so' case doesn't fit
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי אליעזר agrees: in an 'except so-and-so' divorce, once she marries someone else and that marriage ends, she may marry the excluded man.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר agrees about a man who divorces his wife and tells her, 'You are permitted to any man except so-and-so.' If she went and married some ordinary man, and was then widowed or divorced, she is permitted to the man who had been forbidden to her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up what it said in the last step. רבי טרפון's challenge can't be about the 'except so-and-so' divorce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון's challenge was that the first husband's גט would uproot a Torah law forever. But in the 'except so-and-so' case, רבי אליעזר himself says the ban ends once she marries and leaves another husband. So in that case no Torah law is uprooted, and the challenge doesn't fit it.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
Agrees (even though he usually holds otherwise)
An ordinary person (literally 'someone from the market')

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer agrees
regarding one who divorces his wife,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר לָהּ: ״הֲרֵי אַתְּ מוּתֶּרֶת לְכׇל אָדָם,
phrases.english: and said to her: 'You are hereby permitted to any man,
except for so-and-so,'
and she went and married someone from the general public,
and was widowed or divorced,
that she is permitted to the one she had been forbidden to!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind Step 22's rejection of the 'except so-and-so' case.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי טרפון's challenge cannot be about an 'except so-and-so' גט.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי אליעזר agrees that the ban ends after she marries and leaves another man.

steps.title: It must be the 'on condition' divorce
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון's challenge must be about a גט given 'on condition' that she not marry so-and-so.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he was talking about a divorce given 'on condition' (that she not marry so-and-so).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 22. רבי טרפון meant a גט given 'on condition.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A condition does not end when she marries someone else. It stays in force for good. So in that case the husband really could keep her forbidden to the brother forever, and רבי טרפון's challenge fits.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two kinds of גט. 'Except so-and-so' is a limit that ends after she marries someone else. 'On condition' is a lasting condition that never goes away.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי טרפון's challenge (Steps 6 and 15) is about a גט given 'on condition' that she not marry so-and-so, not about one that says 'except so-and-so.'

phrases.english: Rather, it is with regard to 'on condition.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in Step 22, after Step 23 ruled out the other option.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי טרפון was talking about a גט given 'on condition' that she not marry so-and-so.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: forbidden means forbidden to everyone
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי argues against רבי אליעזר. There is no such thing as forbidden to one person and permitted to another.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי הגלילי responded and said: Where do we find something forbidden to this one and permitted to that one? What is forbidden is forbidden to everyone, and what is permitted is permitted to everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes the next rabbi from the ברייתא who argued with רבי אליעזר. This sets up the challenges that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר allows a גט that frees her to everyone except one man. רבי יוסי הגלילי says that kind of split status doesn't exist. Either she is forbidden to all or permitted to all.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili responded and said:

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכָן מָצִינוּ אָסוּר לָזֶה וּמוּתָּר לָזֶה?
phrases.english: Where do we find forbidden to this one and permitted to that one?
What is forbidden is forbidden to everyone,
and what is permitted is permitted to everyone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from רבי טרפון to the next rabbi's refutation in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman cannot be forbidden to one man and permitted to all others. Forbidden is forbidden to all.

steps.title: תרומה and קדשים are forbidden to some and permitted to others
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי הגלילי: תרומה and קדשים are forbidden to non-כהנים but permitted to כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And isn't there such a thing? But תרומה and קדשים are forbidden to this one and permitted to that one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוסי הגלילי's rule with a clear counterexample.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תרומה and קדשים are forbidden to an ordinary Jew but allowed to a כהן. So it is not true that 'forbidden is always forbidden to everyone.'

keyTerms.meaning: The gift of produce given to a כהן
Holy items, such as sacrifice meat

phrases.english: And is it not so?!
But there are תרומה and sacrificial meat,
which are forbidden to this one and permitted to that one!
phrases.notes: 'This one' is a non-כהן and 'that one' is a כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the general rule stated in Step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי הגלילי's rule that forbidden is forbidden to everyone.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תרומה and קדשים prove that the same thing can be forbidden to some people and allowed to others.

steps.title: He meant prohibitions about a woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי הגלילי was only talking about a woman being forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are talking about a woman being forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing רבי יוסי הגלילי's rule to women only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food like תרומה is a different area of law, so it doesn't count. His rule was only about whether a woman may be married.

keyTerms.meaning: We are saying, we are talking about

phrases.english: We are speaking about a forbidden woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the תרומה and קדשים challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule seemed to cover every kind of prohibition.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule only covers prohibitions about a woman.

steps.title: But עריות are forbidden to some men only
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: women forbidden as close relatives are forbidden to some men and permitted to others.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are עריות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second counterexample, this time about women.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman forbidden because of family ties, like a sister, is forbidden to her relative but permitted to other men. So even among women, forbidden is not always forbidden to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Women forbidden because of close family ties

phrases.english: But there are women forbidden as relatives!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the narrowed rule from Step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule as narrowed to forbidden women.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עריות are women forbidden only to certain men, so the narrowed rule still fails.

steps.title: He meant a woman forbidden because she is married
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוסי הגלילי meant a woman forbidden because she is married.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are talking about marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the rule once more. It only covers a woman forbidden because she is married.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A married woman is forbidden to every other man. Once she is divorced, she is permitted to every man. So a גט cannot leave her 'married' toward one man and free toward everyone else, and that is רבי יוסי הגלילי's argument against רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא narrows רבי יוסי הגלילי's rule to a woman forbidden because of marriage. The very next step shows that even this narrowed rule has a hole.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the final, narrowest form of רבי יוסי הגלילי's rule. It is exactly what the גמרא's next challenge (a married woman, permitted to her husband) knocks down.

phrases.english: We are speaking about marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the עריות challenge by narrowing the rule further.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule seemed to cover any woman forbidden for any reason, including relatives.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule only covers a woman forbidden because she is married.

steps.title: But a married woman is forbidden to some and permitted to one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי הגלילי's narrowed claim: a married woman is forbidden to every man except her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about a married woman! She is forbidden to all men and permitted to her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer for רבי יוסי הגלילי. Even a woman forbidden because she is married is permitted to one man, her own husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 29 the גמרא said רבי יוסי הגלילי meant a woman forbidden because of marriage. But that is exactly the kind of woman who is forbidden to everyone and permitted to one person. So his rule, that nothing is forbidden to one and permitted to another, seems to break down again.

keyTerms.meaning: But look at / what about (used here to raise a challenge)

phrases.english: But what about a married woman!
phrases.notes: The point left unsaid: she is forbidden to every man except her own husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רבי יוסי הגלילי meant a woman forbidden because she is married.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A married woman herself is forbidden to all men but permitted to her husband, so 'forbidden to one, permitted to another' clearly exists in this area too.

steps.title: This is the weak point in רבי יוסי הגלילי's argument
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the challenge: this is the refutation of רבי יוסי הגלילי's argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is the refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not try to answer the challenge. It admits that this is the weak point in רבי יוסי הגלילי's argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the סוגיא, רבא said that every challenge against רבי אליעזר except רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's had a weak point. Here the גמרא names the weak point of רבי יוסי הגלילי's challenge: a married woman is a real case of forbidden to all and permitted to one.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation; a weak point in an argument

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי הגלילי's challenge does not fully stand, because a married woman is forbidden to everyone except her husband.

phrases.english: This is the refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 30 as the refutation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The argument of רבי יוסי הגלילי is refuted by the case of a married woman.

steps.title: Which case was רבי יוסי הגלילי talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which kind of divorce רבי יוסי הגלילי meant, and rules out 'on condition', since there she is still permitted to that man outside of marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: In which case was he talking? If you say a divorce 'on condition' that she not marry so-and-so, then she is still permitted to that man in an improper relationship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which divorce case רבי יוסי הגלילי was talking about. It tests one option and shows it does not fit, which sets up the real answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband said 'on condition that you don't marry so-and-so,' the condition only covers marriage. She is not fully forbidden to that man, because relations with him outside marriage would not break the condition. So רבי יוסי הגלילי's words about a woman 'forbidden' to one man cannot fit this case.

keyTerms.meaning: An improper relationship outside of marriage

phrases.english: And in what case?
If you say it was with 'on condition',
but she is permitted to him in an improper relationship!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the refutation, clarifies which case רבי יוסי הגלילי's argument was about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יוסי הגלילי meant a divorce 'on condition' or a divorce 'except for'.

steps.title: He was talking about 'except for so-and-so'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי יוסי הגלילי meant the 'except' case, where she is fully forbidden to that one man.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he was talking about a divorce saying 'you are permitted to everyone except so-and-so.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the answer: רבי יוסי הגלילי meant a divorce that says 'except for so-and-so.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'except,' the גט never frees her from her husband with regard to that one man. So she stays an אשת איש toward him and is fully forbidden to him. That fits the idea of a woman forbidden to one man and permitted to others.

keyTerms.meaning: Except (a divorce that leaves out one man)

phrases.english: Rather, with 'except'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי הגלילי was talking about a divorce worded 'except for so-and-so,' where she remains completely forbidden to that man.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's challenge: she may later marry the forbidden man
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא argues that if she later marries the forbidden man, the גט turns out to be void and her children from the second husband become ממזרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא answered: Suppose she married someone else and had children, then was widowed or divorced, and then married the very man she was forbidden to. Wouldn't the גט turn out to be void and her children ממזרים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי עקיבא's challenge against רבי אליעזר from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא worries about a later chain of events. If she ever marries the man she was excluded from, the גט never really freed her. Then she was still married to her first husband when she married the second man, so the children from that marriage would be ממזרים.

keyTerms.meaning: From the market; any ordinary man
Children born from a forbidden union, such as from a married woman

steps.confusionAlert: The children in danger are NOT from the forbidden man. They are from the middle husband, the one 'from the market', because if the גט is void she was still married when she had them.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva responded and said:
Suppose this woman went
and married some ordinary man
and she had children,
and she was widowed or divorced,
and she then went and married
the man she was forbidden to,
wouldn't the גט turn out to be void
and her children ממזרים?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from רבי יוסי הגלילי's challenge to the next challenge in the ברייתא, from רבי עקיבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גט with this kind of restriction is risky, because a later marriage to the forbidden man would cancel the גט and make her children from the second husband ממזרים. Step 39 shows this argument is about a גט given 'on condition.'

steps.title: Then she could never remarry after any conditional גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא: by his logic, a woman divorced with any condition could not remarry, since she might break the condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then with any ordinary condition she also should not remarry, in case she doesn't keep his condition and the גט turns out void and her children ממזרים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי עקיבא. His worry would apply to every conditional גט, not just this one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many divorces are given with conditions, and the woman is allowed to remarry right away. Each time, she might break the condition later and cancel the גט. Since we do not worry about that in other cases, רבי עקיבא's worry seems to prove too much.

phrases.english: If so,
with all the ordinary conditions
she also should not remarry,
in case she does not fulfill his condition
and the גט turns out to be void
and her children ממזרים!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי בְּכוּלְּהוּ תְּנָאֵי דְּעָלְמָא נָמֵי לָא תִּנְּסִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי עקיבא's argument from step 34.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's worry that a later marriage could cancel the גט.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same risk exists with every conditional גט, yet those women may remarry, so this worry cannot be a reason to reject רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: This is the weak point in רבי עקיבא's argument
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the challenge: this is the refutation of רבי עקיבא's argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is the refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits that this is the weak point in רבי עקיבא's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as with רבי יוסי הגלילי, the גמרא shows that רבי עקיבא's argument against רבי אליעזר has a hole. His worry would forbid remarriage after any conditional גט, which we do not do.
steps.whatToRemember: As רבא said, the challenges of רבי טרפון, רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא all have weak points. רבי טרפון's is the niece case, רבי יוסי הגלילי's is the married woman, and רבי עקיבא's would apply to every conditional גט. Only רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's stands.

phrases.english: This is the refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 35 as the refutation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי עקיבא's argument is refuted, because the same worry would apply to every conditional גט.

steps.title: Which case was רבי עקיבא's objection about? Not the 'except' case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which kind of divorce רבי עקיבא's ממזרים objection referred to. It rejects the 'except' case, because there רבי אליעזר actually permits her to that man.
steps.simpleTranslation: About which case did רבי עקיבא object? If you say the 'except' case, רבי אליעזר actually allows her to marry that man!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי עקיבא's objection from Step 34 and asks which kind of divorce it was aimed at. It immediately rules out the 'except' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא described a woman who ends up marrying the forbidden man, which supposedly makes the גט void. But in the 'except' case, רבי אליעזר himself allows that marriage after she has been married to someone else in between. So an objection built on that scenario cannot be aimed at the 'except' case.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion the גמרא is about to reject)
He fully permits it (a strong way of saying 'permits')

phrases.english: And with regard to what case?
If we say it was the 'except' case,
Rabbi Eliezer actually permits it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְמַאי? אִילֵימָא בְּ״חוּץ״, מִשְׁרָא שָׁרֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי עקיבא's first objection and pins down which case it addressed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Was רבי עקיבא's ממזרים objection about the 'except' case or the 'on condition' case?
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the objection was about the 'except' case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר permits her to the forbidden man in the 'except' case, so there would be nothing to object to.

steps.title: ברייתא: in the 'except' case, רבי אליעזר permits the forbidden man after an in-between marriage
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא proves that in the 'except' case, if she marries someone else and is then widowed or divorced, רבי אליעזר agrees she may marry the man she was forbidden to.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר agreed that if a man divorces his wife and says, 'You are permitted to everyone except So-and-so,' and she marries someone else and is then widowed or divorced, she is allowed to marry the man she was forbidden to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up the claim from the last step that רבי אליעזר permits her to the forbidden man in the 'except' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once she has married someone else and that marriage has ended, she is now leaving that second husband, not the first one. So the first husband's exclusion no longer limits her. This shows the 'except' case leaves no room for רבי עקיבא's ממזרים objection.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees (even someone who usually holds otherwise concedes this point)
Someone from the general public, any ordinary man

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Eliezer agreed
about one who divorces his wife and said to her:
'You are hereby permitted to any man,
except for So-and-so,'
and she went and married someone from the general public
and was widowed or divorced,
that she is permitted to the one she had been forbidden to!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the rejection made in Step 37.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר permits the forbidden man in the 'except' case
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating רבי אליעזר's agreement after an in-between marriage

steps.title: So רבי עקיבא's objection was about the 'on condition' case
steps.stepSummary: Since the 'except' case does not fit, the גמרא concludes that רבי עקיבא was objecting to the 'on condition' case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was about the 'on condition' case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: רבי עקיבא's objection must have been aimed at a divorce given 'on condition' that she not marry So-and-so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the 'on condition' case, marrying that man breaks the condition. That can make the גט void looking backward, which is exactly the scenario where children from the second husband could become ממזרים.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it must be (introduces the correct option)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with Step 33. There, רבי יוסי הגלילי's view was about the 'except' case. Here the גמרא is talking about רבי עקיבא's objection, which fits the 'on condition' case.

phrases.english: Rather, it was the 'on condition' case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 37 after the proof in Step 38.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא's first objection referred to a divorce given 'on condition' that she not marry So-and-so.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's second argument: the forbidden man is a כהן
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא gives another argument: if the forbidden man is a כהן and the first husband dies, she is a widow toward him but a divorcée toward everyone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another argument: suppose the man she was forbidden to is a כהן, and the husband who divorced her dies. Isn't she then a widow toward him and a divorcée toward everyone else?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a second argument from רבי עקיבא against רבי אליעזר's partial גט. This step sets up a strange result that the next step will build on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Toward the forbidden man, the גט never cut the marriage, so she counts as still married to the first husband. When he dies, she becomes a widow toward that man. Toward everyone else she was truly divorced, so she is a divorcée. One woman ends up with two different statuses at once.

keyTerms.meaning: A priest, who is forbidden to marry a divorcée

phrases.english: Another argument:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיָה זֶה שֶׁנֶּאֶסְרָה עָלָיו כֹּהֵן,
phrases.english: Suppose the one she was forbidden to was a כהן,
and the one who divorced her died,
is she not found to be a widow toward him,
and a divorcée toward everyone else?

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: הֲרֵי שֶׁהָיָה זֶה שֶׁנֶּאֶסְרָה עָלָיו כֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first argument was refuted in Step 36, the ברייתא brings רבי עקיבא's second argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With a partial גט, a woman can be a widow toward the excluded כהן and a divorcée toward everyone else at the same time.

steps.title: The קל וחומר: the 'married' status should spread to everyone
steps.stepSummary: A קל וחומר: if the lighter divorcée status forbids her to that כהן, then the heavier married-woman status should forbid her to every man, so the גט cannot work.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is a קל וחומר: if being a divorcée, which is the lighter prohibition, makes her forbidden to that כהן because of the divorced side of her, then being a married woman, which is far more serious, should certainly make her forbidden to everyone!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא finishes his second argument with a קל וחומר showing that the partial גט defeats itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her 'divorced' side toward everyone else reaches the כהן and forbids her to him, even though the divorcée prohibition is minor. So her 'married' side toward that one man, a much more serious prohibition, should reach everyone and forbid her to all men. Then the גט accomplishes nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a heavier one
The 'divorced side' or aspect of her status
A married woman, a very severe prohibition

steps.whyThisMatters: This argument attacks the very idea of a partial גט: a woman cannot be 'married' toward one man without that status affecting everyone.

phrases.english: And it is a קל וחומר:
just as a divorcée, which is a light prohibition,
is forbidden because of the divorced side in her,
a married woman, which is a severe prohibition,
all the more so, isn't it?!
phrases.notes: He means: her 'married' side toward that one man should forbid her to every man.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקַל וָחוֹמֶר: וּמָה גְּרוּשָׁה שֶׁהִיא קַלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a קל וחומר on the double status set up in Step 40.
steps.raayaObject: That a partial גט cannot take effect
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the light divorcée prohibition to the severe married-woman prohibition

steps.title: Which case was the second argument about? Testing the 'on condition' case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which kind of divorce this second argument refers to and begins testing the 'on condition' case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about which case? If you say the 'on condition' case,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question as before, this time about רבי עקיבא's second argument. It starts testing the 'on condition' option, and the answer continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as with the first argument, the גמרא wants to know whether the כהן argument fits the 'except' case or the 'on condition' case. Here it raises 'on condition' first, likely in order to push it aside.

phrases.english: And with regard to what case?
If we say it was the 'on condition' case,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same 'which case?' question from Step 37 to רבי עקיבא's second argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Was the כהן argument about the 'on condition' case or the 'except' case?
